newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil trade balance in equilibrium in January.
newsitem.headline: Brazil trade balance in equilibrium in January.

text.p: Brazil's trade balance for January was in equilibrium and unaffected by problems with a new import registration system, said Mauricio Cortes, secretary of foreign trade at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.

"It was in equilibrium," Cortes told Reuters, denying reports of a surprise January surplus. "The result is absolutely real. Any problems in the first week of the functioning of the SISCOMEX system were fully absorbed in following weeks."
Cortes said importers had increased their purchases in December because of anticipated problems, "even fear" of the SISCOMEX system, which came on line January 1.
"SISCOMEX itself had no effect (on the balance)," he said.
Cortes said he could not put a value on the "influence" anticipated imports in December had had but the January result showed December's record monthly $1.787 billion trade gap was "atypical."
"It is certain the number of imports in December was inflated by anticipated purchases," he said.

Cortes said he was not surprised about the January trade balance, adding that the only people to be surprised were those who had forgotten officials' warnings that importers had anticipated their purchases in December.
"What is important is that January's trade balance was in equilibrium. It's a positive sign in relation to our trade position," he said.
Cortes declined to confirm that up to January 28, Brazil had registered exports of $3.13 billion and imports of $2.91 billion. He also declined to speculate about the trade balance for February.
The Folha de Sao Paulo daily reported Friday that the $222 million surplus posted up January 28 was due to problems with SISCOMEX.

According to internal government documents made available to Reuters, average daily imports in the first week of the month were a miserly $3.3 million, picking up gradually to average $153.1 million by January 28.
It was not until January 15 that imports exceeded $200 million in a single day. In the second week of the month, the highest daily import figure was $91.9 million.
Average daily exports by January 28 were $164.8 million.
A January surplus or even equilibrium would be the first since last May. Brazil posted a record trade gap of $5.54 billion in 1996.
